confounder.rationale: Serum creatinine is clinically plausible as a pretreatment factor that may affect both treatment choice and outcome. Penalized main-effect selection supports this: it was retained for outcome in all analyses and for treatment in most analyses, with clinical background providing additional support for a common-cause role.
evidence_comments: penalized main effects for outcome: nonzero in 3/3 analyses
penalized main effects for treatment: nonzero in 2/3 analyses
clinical background states renal function can influence treatment choice and outcome

effect_modifier.rationale: Evidence for effect modification is weak and not validated. Only one exploratory penalized interaction analysis selected serum creatinine, while univariable R-learner validation showed no improvement over a constant treatment effect. Because the treatment effect of interest is a probability difference and validation R-loss evidence is absent, the available results do not justify using serum creatinine to predict differences in treatment benefit.
evidence_comments: penalized treatment interactions: nonzero in only 1/3 analyses
univariable R-learner validation gains were non-positive in 0/3 analyses
validation R-loss gains were -0.002, 0.0, and -0.001, indicating no validation improvement over a constant effect
